LESSON: READING FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.2: Reading Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Fluency, part of Reading in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can you ensure fluency in reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read a text on formal greetings and introduction,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop an interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read a text on formal greetings and introduction,

   Reading Fluency helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency,

   Reading Fluency helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop an interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.

   Reading Fluency helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read short sentences on formal greetings while observing the correct pronunciation of words,

2. collaborate with peers to circle the particles (harf) in sentences,

3. work jointly to read a dialogue on formal greeting and introduction between two people or groups using appropriate speed and intonation,

4. peer review each other’s reading speed for accuracy,

5. practise reading from a variety of texts for fluency at home.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read short sentences on formal greetings while observing the correct pronunciation of words,
2. collaborate with peers to circle the particles (harf) in sentences,
3. work jointly to read a dialogue on formal greeting and introduction between two people or groups using appropriate speed and intonation,
4. peer review each other’s reading speed for accuracy,
5. practise reading from a variety of texts for fluency at home.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is promoted as the learner engages in collective learning when reading a dialogue on formal greeting

and introduction between two people or groups using appropriate speed and intonation.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is promoted as the learner collaborates with peers to circle the particles (harf) in

sentences.

Values:
Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to peer review each other’s reading speed for accuracy.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is promoted as the learners accommodate and show kindness to each other as they work in groups to

accomplish goals.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can link greetings and introductions to similar concepts also covered in English.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. read a text on formal greetings and introduction,
2. apply appropriate speed and intonation in written texts for fluency,
3. develop an interest in reading Arabic texts for enjoyment.

Remember the key question: How can you ensure fluency in reading?
